quote: We are concerned with the prediction of phrase boundaries from text in a manner that mimics the speech of a fluent child reader.
datasets: Reading Cards created by the Central Institute of English and Foreign Languages (CIEFL), India
outputs: The model outputs are predicted prosodic boundary strengths (continuous), presence/absence of prosodic boundaries (binary), and presence/absence of forbidden pauses (binary).

quote: The full model achieved an R2 of 0.87, RMSE of 0.94, and MAE of 0.57 ... Table 6 summarizes the obtained precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracies.
The full model achieved an R 2 of 0.87, RMSE of 0.94, and MAE of 0.57...
Manual annotation by fluent adult speakers of Indian English was used to obtain the prosodic boundaries in each text.
guideline: Annotators were instructed to mark the boundary words, i.e. words that they would naturally pause after, when reading aloud the presented texts to the children they were meant for.
